title: ArdaNova production-readiness waves
thesis_health: Far. The vocabulary is mostly right — a person signs in with Google, sees 'Account setup', 'Identity check', and 'Managed payment account', and never meets gas, chains, signing, or seed phrases on ArdaNova's screens — and the substrate underneath is careful (single custody chokepoint, fail-closed gates at both dispatch seams, idempotent allocations, honest 'unpriced' analytics). But no thesis moment works end to end in any non-development environment: account setup returns 409 (EnableCustodialAccounts=false, CustodyMode=Disabled, Kyc:Provider=unavailable) and, because no non-development CustodyMode is recognised anywhere in the tree, walletReady is false by construction outside a developer's laptop; a project cannot be edited, published privately, illustrated, or found past the first 50; sponsorship checkout is unreachable by construction (the only settlement gateway is a Retry stub, no project ever gets an assetId, the settlement would mint 'USD' cents as a fresh ASA, and no intent can reach SETTLED); a worker cannot submit a bid from the client, an accepted agreement never advances, escrow is 501/503, the thesis-native off-chain distribute is 501 and admin-only, and payouts are refused at controller and service; voting is a browser alert or a credential nobody can issue; and 'where did the money go' is an admin-only page. Where the UI does function it teaches ARDA, project units, per-ARDA rates, Algorand addresses, transaction hashes, and a Pera/WalletConnect picker in the sidebar. The build order is inverted against the thesis — three chains and a bridge shipped fail-closed while fiat in/out does not exist — and the two repos carry contradictory docs (self-sovereign vs custodial, sidecar vs direct Stripe, a Sybil hole already fixed, tracks marked complete that are 501). The path taken is CHAIN-FIRST, not fiat-first: the review's proposal to put stake in ArdaNova's own ledger with Stripe in and Stripe Connect out, and let AZOA's chain become an anchor later, was put to the owner with its evidence and REJECTED (D44-D47). Fiat is only the ARDA on-ramp and off-ramp; a stake is a real per-project ASA from day one; the node's value primitives — reserve wallet, ARDA genesis, per-project treasury accounts, IssueUnits with custodial recipient preparation, HOLD, consent — are the critical path to the first sponsorship, which lands at the end of Wave 6. Waves 3, 4, 5 and 6 are each multi-session; roughly a quarter of engineering before the first sponsorship, and the worker-paid moment a further two multi-session waves after that.

partitions.note: Per-wave owns_files are in plan.md and were RESET to 'planned' by the 2026-09-07 critique revision, which added W1.8 and W3.7, moved the SDK orchestration deletion from W4.4 to W4.7, moved Stripe-retirement files into W6.1, split the Wave 5 and Wave 6 migrations into two owned-in-order migrations each, and renumbered Wave 8. The earlier proof was the reviewer's hypothesis pinned to 2cd6616 and no longer matches the item list. Every wave's collision proof must be re-verified with a real grep at launch (AC3).

owner_questions_note: The review's Q1-Q4 are answered by D44-D47 and Q5-Q7 are carried as stated assumptions. Of the five design questions D44 opened, D49 and D50 answered two (ARDA genesis; the exchange mechanism), recorded in plan.md as design notes N-X1 and N-X2. Four remain open and gate Wave 3: Q-X2 (the ARDA price per US cent), Q-X3 (project-ASA parameters), Q-X4 (who may create a project token), Q-X5 (the off-ramp destination; Stripe Connect platform approval is an unbounded external clock). Q-X6 (who holds a project's ARDA) is ANSWERED in plan.md - a per-project custodial treasury account on the node - because the waves could not be collision-proofed with it open; the owner may reverse it before W3.7 lands.

revisions.what: chain-first re-sequence under D44-D48; the review's fiat-first ordering rejected

critique pass: all 25 RESEQUENCE-CRITIQUE.json findings applied or accepted by name in plan.md's 'Accepted residual risks'; D49/D50/D51 folded in. Two blockers closed - W1.8 teaches the node a production CustodyMode (walletReady was false by construction outside Development, so every downstream wave was silently blocked on the custody the plan claimed to assume), and W3.7 gives each project a custodial treasury account on the node (the exchange credited the platform reserve, leaving the project's funding balance as the Postgres ledger D47 rejected). Wave 8 reordered so the buy-back liquidity policy lands before the user-facing sell path.
